q: A security team wants developers to find SQL injection and buffer overflow flaws in source code automatically on every commit, before the application is deployed to any environment. Which technique BEST fits?
c: Static analysis integrated into the CI pipeline
Dynamic scanning of the staging environment
An annual external penetration test
Fuzz testing against production endpoints

q: To minimize the cost of fixing security defects, at which point in the software development life cycle should security requirements FIRST be defined?
c: During the requirements phase
During implementation, as code is written
During system testing before release
After deployment, through patching

q: A code review finds user input concatenated directly into SQL statements. Which change MOST effectively eliminates the injection risk?
c: Escaping quote characters in user input
Suppressing database error messages to users
Using parameterized queries for all database access
Limiting the length of every input field

q: A hospital is buying a commercial off-the-shelf clinical application and cannot review its source code. Which approach gives the BEST assurance of the product's security before purchase?
c: A contract clause promising secure coding practices
Independent security certifications and test evidence for the product
An antivirus scan of the installation media
Waiting for other hospitals to report problems

q: A development organization tracks the percentage of code exercised by its security test suite, yet critical vulnerabilities keep shipping from areas the metric rates highly. What is the MOST likely explanation?
c: The coverage tool is miscounting executed lines
All the vulnerabilities are in third-party libraries
Developers are skipping the test suite before release
Coverage shows code was executed, not that security outcomes were asserted

q: A financial services company is designing a new payment-processing microservice. The security architect wants to identify architectural weaknesses, such as missing authentication between services and unprotected data flows, before any code is written. Which activity BEST achieves this goal?
c: Conduct threat modeling of the design using a structured methodology such as STRIDE
Perform dynamic application security testing against a staging deployment
Schedule a manual secure code review once the first release candidate is complete
Commission a penetration test as part of pre-production acceptance

q: During a major outage, a developer pushed a hotfix directly to production, bypassing the normal change approval workflow. The fix resolved the outage. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Roll back the hotfix until it can be processed through the standard change workflow
Invoke the emergency change procedure to document the fix and perform a post-implementation review
Refer the developer to human resources for violating the change management policy
Suspend all production deployments until staff are re-trained on the change process

q: An organization licenses a business-critical application from a small software vendor and is concerned the vendor may go out of business, leaving the application unmaintainable. Which contractual measure BEST addresses this risk?
c: A service level agreement guaranteeing response times for defect fixes
A right-to-audit clause allowing inspection of the vendor's development practices
A source code escrow agreement with release triggers such as vendor insolvency
An extended maintenance contract prepaid for several additional years

q: When a critical vulnerability was disclosed in a widely used open-source logging library, a company needed three weeks to determine which of its applications included the affected component. Which practice would MOST improve its response to similar disclosures?
c: Running static analysis on proprietary source code in every build
Performing authenticated vulnerability scans of all production servers
Deploying a web application firewall rule set updated with new attack signatures
Generating a software bill of materials for every release through software composition analysis

q: A security team must evaluate a web application developed by a contractor who will not provide source code. The application is deployed in a test environment identical to production. Which assessment technique is MOST appropriate?
c: Static application security testing to trace tainted data flows through the code
Software composition analysis to enumerate the application's third-party dependencies
Dynamic application security testing against the running test instance
A documentation review of the contractor's secure coding checklist and sign-offs

q: Auditors find that application developers hold standing administrative access to the production database so they can troubleshoot incidents quickly. What is the BEST way to address this finding?
c: Require developers to sign an acceptable use agreement covering production data handling
Remove standing access and grant time-limited, logged access through a formal request during incidents
Enable full query logging on the production database to record all developer activity
Mask sensitive columns in production so developers see only obfuscated values

q: A threat assessment concludes that an attacker who phishes one developer's repository credentials could introduce malicious code into the main branch of a product that ships to thousands of customers. Which control MOST directly reduces this risk?
c: Branch protection requiring an independent reviewer's approval before any merge to the main branch
Encrypting the repository contents at rest on the code hosting platform
Running a full malware scan of the repository on a nightly schedule
Requiring developers to rotate their repository passwords every 90 days

q: A code review of a discussion forum finds that text submitted in user comments is written into HTML pages exactly as entered. Which secure coding practice MOST directly prevents the resulting vulnerability?
c: Using parameterized statements for all database access from the application
Enforcing TLS for every connection between browsers and the application
Hashing user-submitted content before it is stored in the database
Applying context-appropriate output encoding whenever user data is rendered

q: A security assessment of a privileged utility finds that it verifies a user's permission to a file path and then, a few instructions later, opens that path. Testers demonstrated privilege escalation by replacing the file with a symbolic link between the two steps. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Redesign the code so the permission check and the file operation act atomically on the same file handle
Add strict input validation to reject file paths containing unexpected characters
Run the utility under an account holding the fewest privileges required for its function
Increase audit logging so any file substitution is recorded for later investigation

q: A business-critical network service written in C has a history of memory corruption vulnerabilities. A rewrite in a memory-safe language is budgeted for next year. Which action BEST reduces exploitability in the interim?
c: Obfuscate the compiled binary to make reverse engineering significantly harder
Rebuild the service with stack protection and run it with ASLR and non-executable memory enforced
Digitally sign the executable so that any tampering is detected at load time
Place the service behind a network firewall that permits traffic only to its service port

q: Testers of a customer-facing REST API discover that an authenticated user who changes the numeric account identifier in a request URL receives another customer's account details. The development team proposes fixing the flaw by replacing sequential identifiers with unguessable random values. What is the BEST guidance?
c: Accept the proposal, because unguessable identifiers prevent enumeration of other accounts
Reject the proposal and instead strengthen authentication with multi-factor login
Require the API to verify on every request that the referenced object belongs to the authenticated user
Require the identifiers to be encrypted in transit so they cannot be intercepted and replayed

q: A newly hired CISO must report to the board on how the organization's software security program compares with industry practice and where investment should be prioritized. Which approach BEST supports this reporting?
c: Commission penetration tests of the most critical applications and present the findings
Aggregate vulnerability counts from scanners across all applications into a trend chart
Certify the development organization against ISO/IEC 27001 and report the outcome
Assess the program against a software security maturity model and benchmark the results

q: A development team has completed security testing of a new system that will process regulated health information. Several low-severity findings remain unremediated. Who should decide whether the system may go live with the residual risk?
c: The business owner accountable for the system, through a formal authorization decision
The chief information security officer, because the findings are security defects
The development manager, who best understands the technical impact of the findings
The external auditor who will later assess the system's regulatory compliance

q: A company is retiring a customer relationship management application at the end of its lifecycle. From a security perspective, which activity is MOST important during the disposal phase?
c: Archiving the application's source code repository for future reference
Reassigning the development team promptly to the replacement project
Notifying all users of the retirement date and the migration plan
Sanitizing or migrating stored data in accordance with retention and disposal policy

q: As part of a corporate merger, an organization inherits dozens of custom business applications built by the acquired company, with little accompanying documentation. What should the security team do FIRST?
c: Migrate the applications into the parent company's hardened hosting environment
Require every inherited application to pass a penetration test within 90 days
Inventory the applications and assess each one's criticality, data sensitivity, and exposure
Standardize the inherited codebases on the parent company's approved languages and frameworks

q: A development team is hardening a service that parses image files uploaded by anonymous internet users. The team wants to discover input-handling defects that cause crashes or memory corruption before attackers find them. Which testing technique is BEST suited to this goal?
c: Unit testing with a comprehensive suite of valid sample images
Fuzz testing that feeds the parser large volumes of malformed and mutated inputs
Static analysis of the parser's source code against the coding standard
Regression testing to confirm previously fixed defects have not returned

q: An online retailer's application passed automated static and dynamic scans, yet a customer later obtained goods for free by applying the same discount voucher repeatedly within a single checkout. Which assessment method would MOST likely have discovered this flaw before release?
c: Manual testing driven by abuse cases derived from the application's business rules
Re-running the dynamic scanner with an expanded plugin set and an authenticated crawl
Adding software composition analysis to identify vulnerable third-party libraries
Raising the static analyzer's sensitivity so it reports lower-confidence findings

q: After reviewing recent supply chain attacks, a security architect is concerned that a compromise of the company's build server could insert malicious code into software delivered to customers without any change appearing in the source repository. Which set of controls BEST addresses this threat?
c: Antivirus scanning of build outputs combined with mandatory code review of all source commits
Isolating and hardening the build infrastructure, signing artifacts, and verifying builds are reproducible from source
Multi-factor authentication for repository access combined with secret scanning of the codebase
Deploying the build server in a private subnet protected by a next-generation firewall

q: A hospital runs a browser-based clinical application with a known, remotely exploitable input-handling vulnerability. The vendor has dissolved, no source code is available, and the system cannot be replaced for at least a year. Which compensating control BEST reduces the risk of exploitation?
c: An intrusion detection sensor tuned to alert on attempts to exploit the flaw
A stricter patch management cycle for the server's underlying operating system
A web application firewall with virtual patching rules for the known vulnerability
Full-disk encryption on the server that hosts the clinical application

q: A routine scan of a source code repository discovers that a database administrator password was committed eight months ago. The password is still valid, and dozens of developers and contractors have cloned the repository since then. What should the security team do FIRST?
c: Delete the file containing the password from the repository's current branch
Rewrite the repository history so the commit containing the password is purged
Enable pre-commit secret scanning to block future credential commits
Rotate the exposed password and review database activity for signs of misuse

q: A developer must validate a country-code field that should only ever contain one of the 249 two-letter ISO codes. Which validation approach BEST reflects secure coding guidance?
c: Compare the input on the server against an explicit list of the permitted codes
Reject input on the server that matches a list of known dangerous character patterns
Validate the field in browser JavaScript before the form can be submitted
Accept the input and sanitize it by stripping special characters before use

q: An internal review at an insurance company shows an analyst reconstructed a highly sensitive, access-restricted dataset by combining the results of many individually permitted database queries over several weeks. Which control BEST addresses this type of attack?
c: Row-level encryption of the sensitive tables with keys held by the security team
Context-dependent access control that evaluates a user's accumulated query history
Normalizing the database schema to remove redundant copies of sensitive attributes
Requiring the analyst's manager to approve each database role assignment

q: A development team wants to adopt an open-source authentication library as a core dependency of a new product. Beyond confirming the license is acceptable, which evaluation is MOST important before adoption?
c: Confirming the library is the most widely downloaded option in its category
Relying on its open-source nature, since publicly visible code has already been reviewed by the community
Reviewing the project's maintenance activity, responsiveness to reported vulnerabilities, and disclosure history
Checking that the library compiles cleanly with no warnings in the team's build environment

q: A manufacturing plant depends on a production-scheduling application whose vendor ended all support two years ago. Replacement requires an 18-month project the business has not yet funded, and the security team has flagged the unsupported software as a high risk. What is the MOST appropriate course of action?
c: Insist the application be decommissioned immediately because unsupported software violates policy
Accept continued use without conditions because the application has caused no incidents to date
Transfer the risk by adding the application to the company's cyber insurance schedule
Isolate the system with compensating controls and obtain documented risk acceptance tied to a funded replacement timeline

q: During a pre-release security assessment, a tester discovers an undocumented URL that bypasses authentication and was added by a developer to speed up debugging. Management asks how to prevent similar features from reaching future releases. What is the BEST recommendation?
c: Require peer code review with explicit checks for undocumented functionality before any release is approved
Depend on pre-release penetration testing to find any remaining maintenance hooks
Have every developer sign a policy acknowledging that debugging backdoors are prohibited
Restrict knowledge of production URLs so undocumented endpoints remain unknown to outsiders

q: A development team requests a full copy of the production customer database to reproduce a defect in the test environment. The test environment has weaker access controls and is used by contractors. What is the BEST way to satisfy the team's need while protecting the data?
c: Encrypt the copied data at rest in the test environment using the same keys as production
Require the contractors to sign nondisclosure agreements before granting access to the test environment
Provide a masked or synthetically generated data set that preserves the format and referential integrity of the production data
Restore the production backup to test and delete it as soon as the defect is reproduced

q: An agile development group completes eight two-week sprints and then submits the finished product to the security team for a single pre-release review, which finds serious design flaws requiring extensive rework. What is the BEST way to prevent this from recurring?
c: Integrate security activities such as threat review and secure design checks into every sprint's definition of done
Move the security review earlier, holding it after the fourth sprint instead of the last one
Extend the final security review so the team has more time to fix all findings before release
Require the security team to approve each user story before development work may begin

q: Quarterly application scans keep finding the same cross-site scripting pattern across products built by different development teams. Each team fixes its own findings, but new code keeps reintroducing the flaw. What should the security manager do to address the MOST likely root cause?
c: Increase automated scanning frequency from quarterly to weekly so the flaws are detected sooner
Deploy a web application firewall in front of all products to block cross-site scripting payloads
Create a central remediation team to fix cross-site scripting findings on behalf of the product teams
Publish an organizational secure coding standard with approved output-encoding libraries and train developers on it

q: Business analysts have used a cloud low-code platform to build dozens of workflow applications that process customer data, entirely outside the IT department. The CISO learns of this only after one application emails spreadsheets of customer records to a personal account. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Block the low-code platform at the proxy until every application it hosts is decommissioned
Govern the platform: inventory the applications, enforce guardrails such as connector allow-lists, and require review proportionate to data sensitivity
Require all future business applications to be rebuilt by the IT development team under the standard SDLC
Purchase the platform vendor's premium security add-on so data loss prevention is enforced automatically

q: An organization is starting development of a new network service that will parse untrusted input at high throughput. Its existing C-based services have suffered repeated buffer overflow vulnerabilities. Which decision would MOST effectively reduce this class of vulnerability in the new service?
c: Select a memory-safe programming language for building the new service
Compile the service with stack canaries, address space layout randomization, and non-executable memory
Require fuzz testing of every build in the continuous integration pipeline
Mandate manual code review of all memory allocation and pointer arithmetic

q: A security assessment finds database passwords and API keys hard-coded in the source of many internal services, and configuration files containing credentials checked into version control. Which approach BEST remediates this at the organizational level?
c: Encrypt the configuration files and keep the decryption key in an environment variable on each server
Have developers load credentials from local environment variables instead of committing them to source files
Deploy a centralized secrets management service that issues, rotates, and audits credentials, and scan repositories to remove embedded secrets
Rotate every discovered credential immediately and publish a policy forbidding hard-coded secrets

q: A web application stores its session identifier in a browser cookie. The security team wants to reduce the risk that script injected into a page can read the identifier and that it is ever sent over unencrypted connections. Which control BEST meets both goals?
c: Digitally sign the cookie value so any tampering can be detected by the server
Set the HttpOnly and Secure attributes on the session cookie
Shorten the session timeout so stolen identifiers expire more quickly
Store the session identifier in HTML5 local storage instead of a cookie

q: Customers of an online banking application report transfers they did not initiate. Investigation shows the requests came from the victims' own authenticated browsers while they were viewing an unrelated website, and no malware or credential theft was involved. Which control MOST directly addresses this attack?
c: Context-aware output encoding of all user-supplied content rendered by the application
Upgrading all connections to TLS 1.3 with HTTP Strict Transport Security enabled
Parameterized queries for all data-access code in the transfer functionality
Per-session anti-forgery tokens validated on every state-changing request

q: A penetration test achieves remote code execution on a Java application by submitting a crafted serialized object to an endpoint that deserializes client-supplied data. Patching the specific gadget chain closes the finding, but the security architect wants a durable fix. What should the architect recommend?
c: Stop deserializing native objects from untrusted sources and exchange data in a simple format validated against a schema
Maintain a blocklist of classes used in known gadget chains and reject them during deserialization
Apply TLS to the endpoint so serialized objects cannot be modified by attackers in transit
Run the application in a container so any exploitation is contained within the sandbox

q: During testing, analysts observe that a failed login attempt against a public web application returns a page containing a database stack trace, table names, and the version of the data-access framework. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Suppress all error logging so that sensitive details are never written anywhere
Return the detailed stack trace only when the request originates from the internal network
Return a generic error message to users while recording full diagnostic detail in protected server-side logs
Encode the stack trace so it is not readable in the page source shown by the browser

q: A critical vulnerability found during an application penetration test has been reported as fixed by the development team. Before closing the finding, what should the security team do FIRST?
c: Update the risk register to show the vulnerability as fully remediated
Retest the application to confirm the fix is effective and has not introduced regressions
Obtain sign-off from the business owner accepting any residual risk
Schedule the next annual penetration test to revalidate the entire application

q: The board asks the CISO to demonstrate whether the secure development program is actually improving software security rather than merely generating activity. Which reporting approach BEST answers the board's question?
c: The total number of vulnerabilities found by automated scanning tools in each quarterly period
The number of developers who completed secure coding training during the past year
The count of security testing tools integrated into the CI/CD pipeline this year
Trends in the rate of vulnerabilities escaping to production and mean time to remediate, normalized across releases

q: In a multilevel-secure logistics database, users at a lower classification level discover that certain cargo records cannot be inserted because 'a record with this key already exists', revealing that a classified shipment is present at a higher level. Which database mechanism addresses this inference problem?
c: Polyinstantiation, which permits different tuples with the same primary key at different classification levels
Referential integrity constraints enforced consistently across all classification levels
Database normalization to remove redundant and duplicated data from the schema
Cell suppression applied to published statistical summaries of the database

q: Shortly before launch of a commercial closed-source product, a software composition analysis report shows a statically linked library governed by a strong copyleft license. The library is well maintained and free of known vulnerabilities. What is the MOST significant risk the product team must address?
c: The library may contain undisclosed vulnerabilities that scanners have not yet catalogued
The maintainers may abandon the library, leaving the product without a source of patches
The license may obligate release of the organization's proprietary source code or prevent distribution under its current commercial model
The library may transmit usage telemetry to its maintainers in violation of privacy policy

q: A cloud team provisions all environments from infrastructure-as-code templates. Audits repeatedly find storage buckets deployed with public access and databases without encryption, which the operations team corrects manually after each audit. What is the BEST way to prevent these misconfigurations?
c: Increase the frequency of cloud configuration audits from quarterly to monthly
Add automated policy checks in the pipeline that scan the templates and block noncompliant deployments
Grant the operations team a standing change window so misconfigurations are corrected faster
Restrict console access so engineers cannot modify resources after they are deployed

q: Developers pull container base images directly from public registries into production builds. A recent release shipped with a cryptominer embedded in a popular but tampered public image. Which control BEST prevents a recurrence?
c: Run antivirus scans on the production hosts to detect cryptominers at runtime
Pin each Dockerfile to the 'latest' tag so images always include upstream fixes
Have developers review the source repositories of public images before pulling them
Require builds to use vetted, signed base images from an internal registry that scans and approves them

q: A program office must build a large, novel system with significant technical unknowns, and the sponsor requires that risks be explicitly analyzed and prototypes evaluated before each expansion of project scope. Which development approach BEST matches this requirement?
c: The spiral model, which repeats risk analysis and prototype evaluation in each cycle
The waterfall model, which completes each phase fully before the next phase begins
Rapid application development, which minimizes upfront planning to deliver working software quickly
The V-model, which pairs each development phase with a corresponding testing phase

q: An application security team of three supports more than four hundred developers. Security reviews have become a bottleneck, and product teams increasingly ship without any security input. Budget for additional security hires is unavailable. What is the BEST way to scale security involvement?
c: Require every release to wait in the queue for a full review by the application security team
Purchase an automated scanning suite and discontinue human security reviews entirely
Establish a security champions program that trains a developer in each team to handle routine security work with central support
Outsource all security reviews to an external consultancy engaged for each product release

q: An independent researcher emails a company's general contact inbox describing a serious flaw in its customer portal. The message goes unanswered for three weeks, and the researcher then publishes the details publicly. Which action would BEST prevent a recurrence?
c: Add a legal notice to the website prohibiting unauthorized security testing of its systems
Establish a vulnerability disclosure program with a published intake channel, triage commitments, and response timelines
Contract a private bug bounty platform that is limited to invited researchers only
Route the general contact inbox to the security operations center for continuous monitoring

q: A department wants to connect a third-party scheduling add-on to the corporate email and calendar platform. The add-on requests OAuth permissions to read and send mail for all users and to access all stored files. What should the security team do BEFORE approving the integration?
c: Approve it, since the marketplace vendor was already vetted by the platform provider
Require the vendor to provide source code for internal static analysis before approval
Approve a 90-day trial and review the add-on's audit logs after the period ends
Evaluate whether the requested scopes exceed what the integration needs and constrain the grant to least privilege

q: A web application lets customers upload profile images. A tester uploads a file named avatar.php containing script code, browses to its URL in the upload directory, and executes commands on the server. Which combination of controls BEST prevents this?
c: Validate content and type on the server, store uploads outside the web root under generated names, and serve them through a handler that never executes them
Check the file extension in browser-side JavaScript before allowing the upload to proceed
Scan every uploaded file with antivirus software before saving it to the upload directory
Rename each upload to a random string while keeping its original extension and web-accessible location

q: During rollout planning for newly purchased engineering software, a network review shows the product transmits usage analytics and document metadata to the vendor's cloud by default, and the purchase contract does not address this. What should the security team do FIRST?
c: Block the vendor's cloud endpoints at the perimeter firewall and proceed with the deployment
Accept the transmissions because established vendors routinely anonymize telemetry data
Assess what data is sent against classification and contract requirements, then negotiate configuration or terms before deploying
Deploy now and record the telemetry issue in the risk register for the annual review

q: A file-download feature rejects request paths containing '../', yet a tester retrieves /etc/passwd by sending '%2e%2e%2f' sequences, which the framework decodes after the filter has already run. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Extend the deny-list to cover common encodings such as %2e%2e%2f and double-encoded variants
Canonicalize and fully decode the requested path, then validate that the result resolves inside the permitted directory
Move the file store to a dedicated server so traversal cannot reach operating system files
Enforce HTTPS on the feature so encoded requests cannot be tampered with in transit

q: After releasing version 3 of its public API with strong authentication and rate limiting, a company discovers attackers harvesting customer data through version 1 endpoints that remain online for a few legacy customers and lack those controls. What is the BEST long-term resolution?
c: Add the version 1 endpoints to the web application firewall's monitoring dashboard
Publish documentation instructing all remaining customers to migrate to version 3 promptly
Tighten the rate limits on version 3 to compensate for the exposure of version 1
Migrate the remaining consumers, formally retire version 1, and enforce gateway controls on it until retirement

q: An organization is about to sign a contract for custom software to be developed by an external firm. The security manager is asked when and how software security should be addressed in the engagement. Which answer reflects the BEST practice?
c: Define security requirements, acceptance testing rights, and vulnerability remediation obligations in the contract before development starts
Plan a thorough penetration test of the delivered product during the acceptance phase
Rely on the firm's ISO/IEC 27001 certification as evidence its deliverables will be secure
Request a source code escrow agreement so the code can be reviewed if problems arise later

q: An internal audit finds that application developers compile builds on their own workstations and push them directly into the production environment. Which control BEST addresses the underlying risk this practice creates?
c: Require developers to sign a policy acknowledging that they will deploy only code that has passed all required testing
Mandate peer review of every code change before it is committed to the main branch of the repository
Enforce separation of duties so that an independent release function deploys only artifacts produced by a controlled build pipeline
Grant developers production access only through a jump server that records every session for later review

q: A penetration tester tricks a victim into opening a login page that already carries a session identifier the tester chose. After the victim authenticates, the tester reuses that same identifier and is treated as the logged-in victim. Which coding practice BEST prevents this attack?
c: Generate and issue a completely new session identifier at the moment a user successfully authenticates
Set the HttpOnly and Secure attributes on the cookie that carries the session identifier
Enforce an idle timeout that invalidates any session after a defined period of inactivity
Require a unique anti-forgery token to accompany every state-changing request in the session

q: During a code review of a new customer portal, a reviewer finds that user passwords are stored as unsalted MD5 hashes. Which storage approach should the reviewer recommend instead?
c: Encrypt the password column with AES-256 and protect the encryption key in a hardware security module
Hash each password with a unique salt using a deliberately slow, adaptive algorithm such as Argon2 or bcrypt
Replace MD5 with SHA-256, since MD5 has known collision weaknesses and SHA-256 does not
Base64-encode each password before hashing it so the original value is never processed directly

q: A QA team runs a large automated functional test suite against a staging deployment every night. The application security lead wants vulnerability findings that pinpoint the vulnerable line of code and the runtime data flow that reaches it, gathered passively while those existing functional tests execute. Which technique BEST meets this need?
c: Dynamic application security testing using an active scanner aimed at the staging environment
Static application security testing run against the full source repository on every build
Fuzz testing that feeds malformed input into every externally exposed interface
Interactive application security testing using an instrumentation agent inside the running application

q: An e-commerce checkout page loads a third-party analytics script directly from the vendor's content delivery network. The security team is concerned that a compromise at the vendor could silently turn the script into card-skimming code running in every customer's browser. Which measure BEST mitigates this risk?
c: Confirm the script is always retrieved over TLS so it cannot be modified while in transit to the browser
Place a web application firewall in front of the checkout site to inspect and block malicious payloads
Pin a security-reviewed version of the script and add a Subresource Integrity hash so browsers refuse any altered file
Add contract language obligating the vendor to notify the organization promptly of any compromise

q: A build server compiled malware into a product because the package manager fetched a package from the public registry that had the same name as an internal library but a higher version number. Which change BEST prevents this from happening again?
c: Configure dependency resolution so internal package names are served only from the private registry, and register or scope those names on the public registry
Require developers to manually review the source code of every dependency before each build is allowed to run
Deploy antivirus scanning on the build server so malicious packages are detected when they are downloaded
Pin every dependency to an exact version in a committed lockfile so the build always uses known versions

q: Developers across the organization have started using an AI coding assistant, and executives ask the CISO how the risk of AI-generated code reaching production should be managed. Which approach is BEST?
c: Prohibit AI coding assistants until vendors can certify that generated output is free of vulnerabilities
Rely on the assistant vendor's built-in safety filters, which are designed to suppress insecure suggestions
Require the assistant itself to review and approve the code it generated before developers commit it
Subject AI-generated code to the same review, testing, and composition-analysis gates as human-written code, under an acceptable-use policy

q: After a widely reported incident in which a software vendor's update channel was hijacked to distribute malware, a security manager reassesses how the organization applies updates to a business-critical COTS application. Which practice BEST reduces the risk of installing a poisoned vendor update?
c: Apply each vendor update immediately upon release to keep the window of unpatched vulnerability as short as possible
Verify each update's digital signature and published hash, then stage it in a test environment before promoting it to production
Disable the application's update mechanism permanently and continue operating the currently installed version
Rely on the vendor's most recent SOC 2 report as assurance that its software release process is operated securely

q: A newly purchased engineering application fails at runtime unless users run it with local administrator rights on their workstations, and the business urgently needs the tool in service. What is the security team's BEST course of action?
c: Work with the vendor to identify the specific file, registry, and service rights the application actually needs and grant only those, isolating the tool if that proves impossible
Grant the user accounts local administrator rights but add endpoint detection and response monitoring to identify any resulting abuse
Refuse to deploy the application until the vendor re-engineers it to run without any elevated privileges at all
Provide administrator rights only while the application is being installed and remove them once setup completes

q: A payment module passes 100 percent of its documented test cases, yet an assessor discovers it does not implement a regulator-mandated strong customer authentication requirement because no specification or test for it was ever written. This gap is BEST described as a failure of:
c: Verification, because the software was not built in conformance with its documented specifications
Unit testing, because the individual authentication components were not exercised thoroughly enough
Validation, because the delivered product does not satisfy its intended purpose and stakeholder requirements
Regression testing, because a previously working authentication capability was allowed to break

q: The first full vulnerability scan of an application portfolio yields roughly 14,000 findings, far more than the development organization can remediate this year. As the application security manager, what is the BEST way to direct the remediation effort?
c: Direct all teams to remediate every finding with a critical or high CVSS base score before addressing anything else
Rank findings by exploitability, actual exposure, and the business criticality of each application, and set risk-based remediation targets
Divide the findings evenly across the development teams so each carries a fair share of the remediation workload
Suppress the informational and low-severity findings and rescan the portfolio to establish an accurate baseline count

q: An architect is defining the logging requirements for a new loan-origination application. Which requirement would BEST support future security investigations while limiting the new risk the logs themselves introduce?
c: Capture the full request and response payload of every transaction so investigators always have complete data available
Store the logs on each application server, protected by strict local file permissions from unauthorized access
Record only failed authentication attempts, since successful, authorized activity has no investigative value
Record security-relevant events with actor, timestamp, and outcome, exclude secrets and sensitive fields, and forward logs to a centralized tamper-resistant store

q: An online store's mobile app calculates the order total on the device and submits it to the server, which charges whatever amount arrives. Testers demonstrated paying one cent for a full cart by altering the total with an intercepting proxy. What is the BEST fix?
c: Recalculate the order total on the server from authoritative catalog prices and treat any client-supplied amount as untrusted display data
Obfuscate the mobile application binary so attackers cannot reverse engineer the price calculation logic
Implement certificate pinning in the app so an intercepting proxy can no longer view or modify its traffic
Reject submitted totals that deviate significantly from the customer's historical average order value

q: A code review reveals that a developer wrote a custom stream cipher to protect stored customer data, reasoning that an algorithm nobody has seen is harder to attack. What should the organization's secure coding standard require instead?
c: Publishing the custom algorithm for open community review before it is approved for production use
Doubling the key length used by the custom cipher to make brute-force attacks computationally infeasible
Using vetted, widely reviewed cryptographic libraries that implement approved standard algorithms rather than any custom cryptography
Compressing the data with a proprietary scheme before encryption so patterns are hidden from analysis

q: Months after an outsourced development engagement ended, a routine review finds that the contractor's accounts still hold write access to the organization's source repositories and CI/CD system. Beyond disabling the accounts, what is the BEST way to prevent this from recurring?
c: Require all contractors to sign nondisclosure agreements that define their obligations after the engagement ends
Migrate the repositories to new internal URLs at the close of every engagement so former contractors cannot locate them
Audit the full repository commit history to confirm the contractor made no unauthorized changes after the engagement ended
Tie development-ecosystem accounts into the joiner-mover-leaver deprovisioning process and periodically recertify all repository and pipeline access

q: Two weeks before a contractually committed launch date, the program director instructs the security team to cancel the planned penetration test of a new customer portal so the schedule can be met. What should the security manager do FIRST?
c: Escalate to the board of directors that the program director is attempting to violate the organization's security policy
Document the risks of releasing the portal untested and present them to the accountable business owner for an informed risk decision
Proceed with the launch and quietly schedule the penetration test to run against the portal shortly after go-live
Refuse the instruction and invoke the security policy's authority to block any release that has skipped required testing

q: A payments platform must release a substantial rewrite of its transaction-processing engine. Testing has been thorough, but the team acknowledges that some failure modes will appear only under real production traffic. Which deployment approach BEST limits the risk of the release?
c: Release progressively to a small percentage of live traffic with automated health monitoring and an immediate rollback path before expanding further
Deploy to all users at once during the lowest-traffic overnight maintenance window to minimize how many transactions are affected
Keep extending the staging test campaign until the team is confident every remaining failure mode has been identified
Deploy fully to production with a rehearsed emergency change procedure standing by in case a failure occurs

q: A marketing feature lets staff create email templates whose placeholder expressions are evaluated by the server-side template engine at send time. A researcher demonstrates that a crafted placeholder executes operating system commands on the mail server. Which remediation BEST addresses the root cause?
c: Add an input filter that strips known dangerous keywords and characters from submitted template expressions
Run the template-rendering service under a low-privilege account so injected commands gain minimal access
Render user-authored templates with a sandboxed or logic-less template engine that cannot reach code execution, treating template content as untrusted input
Deploy a web application firewall rule set tuned to detect and block command-injection payload signatures

q: Before promoting a newly built application server into production, an engineer works through the deployment checklist. Which step BEST reduces the server's attack surface?
c: Enable verbose logging across all services so any future attack is captured in maximum detail
Remove sample applications and default accounts, and disable every service and module the application does not require
Install the latest antivirus engine and signature updates before the server is exposed to traffic
Schedule the server for weekly authenticated vulnerability scans once it enters production

q: A data science team's proof-of-concept application, built without security involvement, has quietly become a system the sales force uses daily with live customer data. The CISO discovers this during an unrelated review. What is the BEST way to handle the situation?
c: Shut the application down immediately and require it to restart a full development life cycle from the requirements phase
Permit continued use, since the application has operated for months without any security incident being reported
Direct the data science team to self-assess the application against the organization's secure coding standard
Assess the application's risk in its current state, apply controls proportionate to the data it handles, and bring it under formal SDLC governance

q: A department head asks IT to install a free file-conversion utility, downloaded from a small independent developer's website, on fifty corporate workstations. Which action should the security team take FIRST?
c: Evaluate the software's provenance and behavior, checking the publisher's signature and reputation and observing it in an isolated analysis environment, before approving deployment
Approve the installation, since the utility is free, widely downloaded, and requested by a department head
Purchase a commercial alternative instead, because commercially licensed software carries stronger assurance by default
Install the utility on a single production workstation and monitor its behavior for a week before the wider rollout

q: Shortly after a public product-search API launches, scripted clients begin sending thousands of requests per second, degrading service for legitimate integration partners. Which control MOST directly addresses this abuse?
c: Require registered API keys so that every calling application is uniquely identified in the request logs
Enforce per-client rate limits and usage quotas at the API gateway, returning throttling responses when thresholds are exceeded
Configure auto-scaling so that additional server capacity automatically absorbs the extra request volume
Publish an acceptable-use policy defining the request volumes that API consumers are permitted to send

q: Six months after a cross-site scripting flaw was fixed and the fix verified, a routine assessment finds the identical flaw reintroduced by a user-interface refactor. Which improvement to the testing program BEST prevents this class of recurrence?
c: Commission an annual penetration test of the application by an external firm with web expertise
Require a senior developer to manually review every user-interface change before it can be merged
Add automated security regression tests to the CI suite that specifically assert previously fixed vulnerabilities remain fixed
Re-baseline the static analysis scanner after each release so that new findings stand out from old ones

q: During an outage investigation, engineers discover that the production binary of a core service matches no build in the artifact repository: someone patched it directly on the server months earlier, and the change appears nowhere in version control. Which discipline was MOST fundamentally lacking?
c: Vulnerability management, because routine scanning of the server should have detected the modified binary
Incident management, because the original problem that prompted the direct fix was never handled as an incident
Privileged access management, because engineers should not hold accounts capable of altering production servers
Software configuration management, because every production change must be versioned, authorized, and reproducible from controlled sources

q: An assessor asks a project team to demonstrate that every security requirement approved at the start of a development project was actually carried through design, implemented in code, and proven by testing. Which artifact BEST provides this evidence?
c: The final penetration test report showing which vulnerabilities were discovered and how each was remediated
A requirements traceability matrix linking each security requirement to its design elements, implementing modules, and test cases with results
The threat model produced during architecture design, listing the threats the team considered and the mitigations chosen
The continuous integration logs proving that the automated test suite passed on the final release build

q: A B2B invoicing platform accepts XML documents uploaded by trading partners. A penetration tester submits an invoice whose DOCTYPE declaration defines an external entity, and the parsed response returns the contents of a server configuration file. Which remediation BEST addresses the root cause?
c: Deploy a web application firewall rule that rejects any upload containing the string "DOCTYPE"
Validate every uploaded invoice against the published XML schema after the document has been parsed
Configure the XML parser to disable document type definitions and external entity resolution
Require TLS with mutual authentication for all partner uploads so documents cannot be altered in transit

q: A marketing feature lets users submit a URL that the web server fetches to build a link preview. A security review warns that the server, hosted on a cloud instance, could be induced to request the cloud metadata service and expose the instance's role credentials. Which control BEST mitigates this risk?
c: Validate submitted URLs against an allow-list of approved external destinations and block server egress to internal, private, and link-local address ranges
Require users to authenticate with multi-factor authentication before they are permitted to submit URLs to the link preview feature
Add the metadata service address 169.254.169.254 to a deny-list that is checked against the URL string the user submits
Enable detailed logging of every outbound request the preview service makes so the security operations team can investigate abuse

q: An assessor reviewing a retail bank's customer API finds that it reflects any Origin request header value into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. What is the MOST significant consequence of this configuration?
c: TLS certificate validation is disabled for cross-origin calls, letting attackers intercept API traffic on the network
Origin header values reflected into responses give attackers a way to inject SQL into backend database queries
Legitimate partner sites on other origins will be blocked by browsers, creating an availability problem for integrations
Any malicious website a logged-in customer visits can issue credentialed requests and read that customer's API responses in the browser

q: Testing shows that a web application's fund-transfer confirmation page can be loaded inside an invisible iframe on an attacker's site, where a disguised button tricks victims into clicking the real "Confirm" control. Which control MOST directly prevents this attack?
c: Anti-forgery tokens embedded in every state-changing fund-transfer request
A frame-ancestors Content-Security-Policy directive that stops other sites from framing the page
Setting the HttpOnly attribute on the application's session cookie
Server-side revalidation of the transfer amount and destination account number

q: A tester logged in as a standard user manually browses to /admin/exportAllCustomers, a URL never shown in the standard user interface, and receives a full customer database export. Which flaw does this demonstrate?
c: The application hides privileged links in the interface instead of enforcing server-side authorization on each administrative function
Session identifiers are insufficiently random, allowing a standard user to guess and take over an administrator's session
The export function fails to validate its input parameters before executing the underlying database query
Customer records are stored without field-level encryption, so any retrieval exposes them in cleartext

q: A mobile banking app displays only account nicknames and balances, but an intercepting proxy shows the backend API returns each customer's full profile — including tax identifier and date of birth — which the app discards before display. What should the security team recommend?
c: Obfuscate the mobile application binary so attackers cannot easily discover the API endpoints it calls
Implement certificate pinning in the app so API responses cannot be intercepted by a proxy
Redesign the API so the server returns only the data elements each client function actually requires
Encrypt the sensitive JSON fields using a key embedded within the mobile application package

q: A billing system written in C multiplies usage units by unit price into a 32-bit signed integer. A customer submitted an extremely large usage value, the computed total wrapped to a negative number, and the system issued an account credit. Which change MOST directly prevents this defect class?
c: Widen the total field to a 64-bit signed integer so that much larger products can be represented
Range-check inputs against business-plausible limits and perform monetary calculations with overflow-checked arithmetic
Use parameterized statements for all inserts and updates issued by the billing engine
Enable stack canaries, ASLR, and non-executable memory protections on the billing servers

q: Investigating a breach, analysts find forged entries in the application's authentication log. The application writes the user-supplied username directly into the log, and the attacker submitted usernames containing newline characters followed by fabricated log lines to bury evidence of a brute-force attack. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Forward all application logs to write-once storage so recorded entries cannot be modified after the fact
Tighten file system permissions so that only the logging service account can write to the log files
Stop recording user-supplied values such as usernames in the application's security logs altogether
Encode or sanitize user-supplied values — stripping control characters or using structured formats — before writing them to logs

q: A penetration tester demonstrates account takeover by predicting password-reset tokens, which the application derives from the request timestamp using a standard library pseudo-random function. Which change BEST eliminates the vulnerability?
c: Generate single-use, short-lived reset tokens from a cryptographically secure random number generator with sufficient entropy
Hash each generated token with SHA-256 before including it in the emailed password-reset link
Increase the token length to 64 characters while keeping the existing generation routine unchanged
Ensure that password-reset links are only ever delivered over TLS-protected connections

q: A security researcher decompiles a retailer's published mobile app and extracts a single embedded API key that grants write access to the backend pricing service for every installation. The exposed key has already been rotated. What is the BEST architectural change to prevent recurrence?
c: Apply commercial-grade obfuscation to the app binary so the replacement key is much harder to locate
Ship the key encrypted within the app package and have the app decrypt it in memory at startup
Replace the shared embedded key with per-user authenticated sessions and enforce privileged pricing operations on the server
Implement certificate pinning so the app's API traffic cannot be intercepted and the key cannot be captured in transit

q: In a containerized platform, the internal payments service accepts any request originating inside the cluster network without authentication because "only trusted services run there." A compromise of one low-value service allowed testers to invoke payment operations directly. Which design change BEST corrects the underlying weakness?
c: Move the microservices onto a more tightly segmented internal network with stricter firewall rules between zones
Require every service-to-service call to present a verified service identity — for example mutual TLS — and authorize each request regardless of network origin
Deploy a web application firewall at the internet edge to inspect all traffic entering the cluster
Encrypt all east-west traffic with TLS using a single wildcard certificate shared across the cluster's services

q: An architect is designing a document-signing platform expected to remain in service for more than fifteen years and asks how the design should account for the likelihood that currently approved signature algorithms will be deprecated during that lifetime. Which approach BEST addresses this concern at design time?
c: Select the largest key sizes available today so the chosen algorithms will never require replacement during the platform's life
Develop a proprietary in-house signature algorithm, reasoning that attackers cannot analyze what has never been published
Plan to rewrite the cryptographic layer as a dedicated project whenever a deprecation announcement is eventually made
Isolate cryptographic operations behind a configurable provider interface and record algorithm identifiers with each signature so algorithms can be replaced without redesign

q: During requirements review for a new mobile feature, the product team proposes continuously collecting customers' precise location because the data "may be useful for future features." The privacy officer objects. What should the development organization do?
c: Limit collection to data needed for defined feature purposes and record retention limits as explicit requirements
Proceed with the collection but require the location history to be encrypted both at rest and in transit
Proceed with the collection but anonymize the stored location history after twelve months of retention
Proceed after adding blanket consent language to the license agreement covering all possible future uses

q: A medical-device firm will build firmware whose requirements are fixed by regulation, must produce documented verification evidence for each development stage, and will undergo a single formal certification before release. Which development approach BEST fits this project?
c: Scrum, delivering the firmware in two-week sprints with a backlog reprioritized as requirements evolve
The spiral model, structuring the project as repeated risk-analysis-driven prototype iterations
A sequential V-model lifecycle in which each specification phase is paired with a corresponding verification and validation stage
DevOps continuous deployment, releasing firmware updates automatically several times per day

q: An insurer is selecting a firm for custom development of a claims system. The security manager wants evidence that a bidder's development process is defined, repeatable, and measured across the organization rather than dependent on a few skilled individuals. Which evaluation criterion BEST provides that evidence?
c: The number of bidder staff holding individual secure-software certifications such as CSSLP
An independent appraisal of the bidder's process maturity, such as a current CMMI maturity level rating
A penetration test report showing few findings for one product the bidder previously delivered
The bidder's ISO/IEC 27001 certification covering its own information security management system

q: A company purchases a human-resources application that can either maintain its own local username and password store or federate with the enterprise identity provider via SAML. From an access-risk perspective, which deployment choice is BEST?
c: Use local accounts configured with strong password complexity, history, and lockout requirements
Use local accounts and have HR managers recertify the application's account list every quarter
Use local accounts synchronized nightly from the corporate directory by an automated batch job
Federate authentication to the enterprise identity provider so central MFA and automated joiner-mover-leaver deprovisioning govern access

q: During resilience testing, engineers discover that when the central authorization service is unreachable, the document management application grants every access request instead of blocking users until the service recovers. Which secure design principle does this behavior violate?
c: Fail securely, because an error condition should cause the system to default to denying access
Least privilege, because users should hold only the minimum rights their job roles require
Separation of duties, because no single component should both request and approve access
Defense in depth, because multiple overlapping layers of controls should protect the documents

q: A reporting application connects to the finance database with an account granted SELECT on every table, including identifiable payroll data, although its reports use only aggregated totals. Auditors demand the exposure be reduced. Which database-level change BEST enforces the requirement?
c: Enable transparent database encryption so that all of the finance data files are encrypted at rest
Grant the reporting account access only to views or stored procedures exposing the required aggregates, and revoke its direct table privileges
Turn on database activity monitoring to alert whenever the reporting account queries payroll tables
Modify the reporting application's queries so that they select only the aggregate columns from the tables

q: A developer wraps the debit and credit steps of a funds transfer in a single database transaction so that if the credit step fails, the earlier debit is automatically rolled back. Which transaction property is the developer relying on?
c: Durability, which guarantees that committed changes survive subsequent system failures
Isolation, which prevents concurrent transactions from interfering with one another
Atomicity, which ensures all steps of a transaction complete or none of them take effect
Consistency, which ensures transactions move the database between valid rule-compliant states

q: A cloud function that resizes uploaded images runs under an execution role with read-write access to every storage bucket and database in the account, because that role "already existed." What should the security team require?
c: Relocate the function into a dedicated cloud account while continuing to use the existing role
Enable detailed logging of every API call that the function's execution role makes to cloud services
Scan each uploaded image for malware before the resizing function is allowed to process it
Assign the function a purpose-built role scoped to only the specific buckets and operations it needs

q: While refactoring the payroll system, a developer discovers code that will corrupt payment records if a particular employee identifier ever disappears from the HR feed — apparently planted by a developer who left last year. The developer offers to simply delete the block and redeploy. What should the application security manager direct FIRST?
c: Invoke the incident response process, preserving the code, repository history, and build records as evidence before any cleanup
Delete the malicious block immediately and redeploy so that the trigger condition can never fire
Add an automated test asserting the trigger condition is handled safely, then schedule the fix in the next sprint
Refer the matter to law enforcement and take no internal action until investigators respond

q: Customers of a helpdesk platform can set their own display names. Support managers routinely export ticket lists to CSV and open them in a spreadsheet program. A tester registers a display name beginning with "=" and demonstrates command execution on a manager's workstation when the export is opened. Which remediation BEST addresses the flaw?
c: Scan all generated export files with antivirus software before offering them for download
Escape or prefix exported cell values that begin with characters such as =, +, -, or @ so spreadsheets treat them as text
Apply HTML entity encoding to customer display names before writing them into the exported file
Restrict the ticket export feature to a much smaller group of senior support managers

q: A phishing campaign distributes links to a company's genuine portal in the form https://portal.example.com/login?next=..., where the next parameter accepts any URL. After authenticating on the real site, victims are silently forwarded to a look-alike page that asks them to re-enter their credentials. Which fix BEST addresses the vulnerability?
c: Add anti-forgery tokens to the portal's login form submission process
Run an awareness campaign teaching users to inspect the address bar carefully after every login
Validate the next parameter against an allow-list of internal relative paths or mapped identifiers before redirecting
Maintain a deny-list of known malicious domains and refuse any redirect that matches an entry

q: Before a high-risk trading application is released, the QA lead proposes that the developers who wrote each module also perform its security testing, since they understand the code best. Why should the security manager object to this arrangement?
c: Security testing must always be performed by an external third-party firm in order to be valid
Developers cannot test effectively because they lack access to the production data set
Manual testing by any human is inferior to automated scanning tools regardless of who runs it
Authors share the assumptions embedded in their code, so objective assessment requires testers independent of the developers

q: The CISO commissions a penetration test of a revenue-critical e-commerce platform, but the operations director objects that testing could disrupt production during the approaching holiday peak. What is the BEST way for the security manager to proceed?
c: Establish documented rules of engagement with the system owner — scope, prohibited techniques, testing windows, emergency contacts — and run the riskiest cases against a production-equivalent staging environment
Postpone all penetration testing until the holiday peak has passed, accepting that the platform enters its highest-exposure period unassessed
Proceed with a full unannounced test against production, since only fully realistic conditions produce meaningful penetration test results
Substitute an automated vulnerability scan for the penetration test because scanning poses far less operational risk to production systems
